sentences.text: Cedarosaurus was a small-sized sauropod that possessed the typical nasal crest of brachiosaurids and had long front legs compared to its hind legs.
The average humerus of Cedarosaurus measured 1380 millimeters and the femur 1395 millimeters.
The ratio of the radius's minimum circumference to its length is 0.31 in Cedarosaurus.
The neural spines of the middle tail vertebrae in Cedarosaurus slant forward when the vertebrae are aligned.
In 2001, researchers published a study on 115 gastroliths found associated with a Cedarosaurus specimen.
The total mass of the gastroliths was 7 kilograms, with the lightest stone weighing 0.1 gram while most weighed 715 grams.
Fossils of Cedarosaurus were discovered in 1996 in eastern Utah within the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation.
Cedarosaurus was officially named and described by Tidwell, Carpenter, and Brooks in 1999.
Cedarosaurus fossils come from the Yellow Cat Member of the Cedar Formation in western Utah and the Paluxy Formation in Texas, USA.
The genus name Cedarosaurus refers to the discovery location, while the species name honors Carol Weiskopf.
Researchers suggest the high surface area of the largest gastroliths indicates they may have helped grind or crush ingested plant material.
The gastroliths were composed mainly of chert, with some sandstone, limolite, and quartz grains also included.
Cedarosaurus belongs to the family Brachiosauridae, which is distinctive for having femur and humerus bones of nearly the same size.
Cedarosaurus belongs to the parent group Brachiosauridae, is classified in the family Brachiosauridae, and is classified in the class Saurischia.
The type species of the genus Cedarosaurus is Cedarosaurus weiskopfae.

Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Cedarosaurus could reach a maximum length of 15 meters and a mass of 10 metric tons. Cedarosaurus lived from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, between 137.05 and 110.1 million years ago.
